result.title: Conditional Optimal Transport and Triangular Maps for Imitation Learning
result.summary: We introduce a unified formulation of imitation learning from demonstrations as a conditional sampling problem solved by triangular transport: a policy is the second block of a triangular map that transports a reference distribution to the conditional distribution of the action chunk given the observation history. Unlike in Diffusion Policy, where it is a fixed Gaussian, the reference becomes a design variable; we take it to be the empirical distribution of the demonstrated action chunks and introduce three instances of the formulation: an optimal transport policy (OTP), a flow matching policy (FMP), and a stochastic interpolant policy (SIP). On the Push-T and robomimic Square tasks, the three policies are competitive in task performance with Diffusion Policy and Consistency Policy while using considerably smaller networks and shorter training, and the informative reference accounts for a substantial part of their performance when few network evaluations are used. The three instances offer different trade-offs rather than a single best method: OTP generates an action chunk with a single evaluation of the smallest network (0.23 million parameters on Push-T) and is suitable for settings in which inference time and model size matter, whereas SIP attains the highest scores among the proposed policies at a higher cost.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文把模仿学习表述为条件采样问题，用三角映射把参考分布搬运为「观测历史→动作块」的条件分布，并给出最优传输、flow matching 与随机插值三种实例；在 Push-T 与 Square 上与 Diffusion Policy 竞争，且网络更小、训练更短。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心线索是把参考分布从固定高斯改为示范经验分布、从而在极少网络评估下仍保持条件多模态采样，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 推理状态如何以数据/证据构成的参考分布初始化与少步生成。
